title: Violin Concerto in D minor
hook: The only concerto by a composer who had once dreamed of becoming a violin virtuoso himself.

painting.title: Lake Keitele
painting.pairingNote: A Finnish lake painted in 1905, the year the revised concerto was first played, by Sibelius’s friend Gallen-Kallela; long streaks of wind cut across the still surface as the violin’s line cuts across the soft strings.

facts: Sibelius trained as a violinist and as a young man wanted, in his own words, to be a celebrated violinist at any price. He realised he had started too late. This is the only concerto he wrote, and it is for his own instrument.
The first version, played in Helsinki on 8 February 1904, was a failure: it was finished too late and was very hard to play. Sibelius withdrew it, cut it and revised it.
The revised version, the one played today, was first heard in Berlin on 19 October 1905, with Karel Halíř as soloist and Richard Strauss conducting.
The orchestra is a full partner, almost as in a symphony. In the first movement a long [[cadenza|cadenza]] for the violin alone takes the place of the middle section, the [[development|development]].
bigPicture.inOneLine: a lonely song over quiet strings (I), a warm, dark hymn (II), a stamping dance that Donald Tovey called “a polonaise for polar bears” (III).

movements.heading: Allegro moderato
movements.summary: The violin enters almost at once, alone and high above a soft cushion of strings, with a long, cool melody. The movement alternates between the soloist and big, dark passages for the orchestra. At its centre the violin plays alone for several minutes, and the movement ends at top speed.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, cool and wide
mainIdeas.description: a long melody for the violin over very soft strings, echoed by a clarinet.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, warm and heroic
mainIdeas.description: a broader melody that rises to passionate octaves.

stops.hear: Very soft, pulsing strings; the violin enters with a long, slow melody high above them
A clarinet echoes the violin’s opening phrase
The violin climbs to a high, passionate note, then turns to a darker tune low on its lowest string; runs, chords and [[double-stop|double stop]]s follow
stops.happening: The theme grows, then a first short [[cadenza|cadenza]]

stops.hear: The full orchestra enters with a dark, surging passage; bassoons and clarinets carry it on
The violin returns with a warmer, broader melody that rises to passionate octaves
Another loud, heavy orchestral passage
stops.happening: The orchestra leads into the cadenza

stops.hear: The violin alone for several minutes: rushing notes, chords and leaps
stops.happening: The long cadenza, in place of the [[development|development]]

stops.hear: Low woodwinds bring back the opening melody while the violin winds around it
The broad heroic melody returns, a little higher than before
stops.happening: Theme 2, now a semitone higher, in B minor

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: Fast and fierce: octaves, leaps and high, glassy notes; the movement ends with one strong D

notice: Listen to how quietly the concerto begins. The violin’s first note emerges from almost nothing.
In the long cadenza there is no orchestra at all, yet the music keeps developing the themes. It is the movement’s middle section, played by one instrument.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Hilary Hahn recorded the concerto in Stockholm in March 2007 with Esa-Pekka Salonen, a Finnish conductor and composer. Her tempi are broad, so the first movement lasts over 17 minutes. On the Spotify album Schoenberg’s Violin Concerto comes first; the Sibelius is tracks 4–6.

movements.heading: Adagio di molto
movements.summary: A slow, song-like movement. After a short phrase in the woodwinds, the violin sings a long melody over plucked strings. The orchestra interrupts with a stormy passage, the violin answers with restless double stops, and the melody returns at a warm climax before the movement fades.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a long, warm melody for the violin, with dark brass chords underneath.

stops.hear: Clarinets and oboes play a short, soft phrase in pairs
The violin sings a long, warm melody over plucked strings, with dark chords in the brass
The orchestra breaks in loudly with the opening phrase; the mood turns stormy
The violin answers with restless [[double-stop|double stop]]s, then rippling notes that climb to a long [[trill|trill]]
stops.happening: The violin pushes towards the climax

stops.hear: Violin and orchestra together reach a climax on the main melody

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The violin floats up to a soft, high note; quiet chords in B-flat major close the movement

notice: Listen under the violin’s song in the first minutes. The brass chords do not simply support the melody: they rub against it, which gives the warmth a shadow.

movements.heading: Allegro, ma non tanto
movements.summary: A heavy, stamping dance. Timpani and low strings set up a rhythm and the violin enters with a bold tune on its lowest string. A swaying second tune in the orchestra brings contrast, and the violin shows off in every way possible on the way to the end.

mainIdeas.name: The stamp
mainIdeas.description: a rhythm in timpani and low strings, one long note and two short.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a bold, rugged tune on the violin’s lowest string.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a swaying, waltz-like tune, first in the orchestra.

stops.hear: Timpani and low strings stamp out a rhythm: long, short-short
The violin enters with a bold tune, played low on its lowest string
The orchestra sweeps into a swaying, waltz-like tune in G minor
The violin takes up the swaying tune with leaping [[arpeggio|arpeggio]]s and double stops
The stamping rhythm and the bold tune return
The swaying tune again, now in D minor
High, whistling notes on the violin, then hard, biting chords

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Leaping octaves and double stops; a scale up and back down; one final D for everyone

notice: Count along with the opening: one long, two short. The rhythm keeps returning under the violin and gives the whole movement its heavy tread.

threads.title: A violinist’s concerto
threads.body: Sibelius gave up his hopes of a solo career, but the concerto shows how well he knew the instrument: its dark low string, its high register and its fireworks.

threads.title: Symphonic, not just a showpiece
threads.body: The orchestra has long passages of its own, and the first movement’s cadenza does real musical work.

threads.title: Darkness to D major
threads.body: The concerto begins in a cool D minor and ends in a stamping D major.
